verses.text: Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king after him.

David said, "I will be kind to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father was kind to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him about his father's death. When David's officials came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to comfort him,

the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, "Do you really think David is honouring your father by sending these men to comfort you? No, his officials have come to explore the land, spy on it, and find a way to destroy it!"
So Hanun grabbed David's officials, shaved their beards, cut off their robes in the middle at the hips, and sent them away.

When someone told David what had happened to these men, he sent messengers to meet them, because they were deeply ashamed. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, and then come home."

The Ammonites realised that they had made David hate them. So Hanun and the Ammonites sent about thirty-four thousand kilograms of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, from Aram Maacah, and from Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah came with his army and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites also gathered from their towns and came out to fight.
When David heard about this, he sent Joab with the whole army of mighty warriors.
The Ammonites marched out and lined up for battle at the entrance of their city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country.
Joab saw that there were enemy lines in front of him and behind him. So he chose some of the best soldiers in Israel and lined them up against the Syrians.
He put the rest of the army under the command of his brother Abishai, and they lined up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, you must come and help me. But if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will come and help you.
Be brave! Let's be strong for our people and for the towns of our God. May the LORD do what he thinks is best."
Then Joab and the troops with him marched out to fight the Syrians, and the Syrians ran away from him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Syrians were running away, they also ran away from Joab's brother Abishai and went back into their city. Then Joab went back to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians saw that Israel had defeated them, they sent messengers to bring more Syrian troops from beyond the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
When David was told about it, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and marched toward them. He lined up his army against the Syrians, and they fought against him.
But the Syrians ran away from Israel. David killed seven thousand of their chariot drivers and forty thousand of their foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the commander of their army.
When Hadadezer's servants saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his servants. After that, the Syrians were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.
